_readme: The DDCS Studio header wordmark, DECLARED. brand/trace-wordmark.py is a DUMB INTERPRETER of this file — it holds no font/size/colour/shear constants of its own. Every mark is two lines: the 'DDCS' wordmark and the 'CNC MACRO STUDIO' tagline, each made of one or more coloured LAYERS (a layer = one traced line of text, offset/coloured/filtered independently — a mark with a bevel or a glow just stacks more than one layer of the same text). Regenerate a mark by re-running trace-wordmark.py against this file; never hand-edit a MARK-*-TRACED.svg's path data directly.
traps: SHEAR SIGN IS NEGATIVE: sh = -tan(radians(slantDeg)). The y-flip in scale(s*xscale, -s) runs BEFORE the shear in the transform chain, so a positive shear leans the letters the WRONG way. Assert it: transform a point at cap height (e.g. y=700 in font units) and confirm the resulting x-delta from the baseline point is POSITIVE (leans right). This shipped wrong once.

GOOGLE FONTS WOFF2 FETCH: the URL must carry '&text=DDCS%20CNC%20MACRO%20STUDIO' (every glyph either line uses) AND a MODERN User-Agent string. An old/absent UA gets EOT instead of WOFF2; omitting &text= gets a Cyrillic subset with no 'D' in it at all. Both actually happened. The response's font url does NOT reliably end in '.woff2' either — a live Sniglet response came back as a '/l/font?kit=...' endpoint with no file extension at all; match any fonts.gstatic.com url(), don't require a literal suffix (t2163, also actually happened).
SYSTEM FONTS (normal/studio/futuristic/steampunk) load from %WINDIR%/Fonts/ariblk.ttf, arialbd.ttf, georgiab.ttf directly via fontTools — no fetch, no &text= concern.

'fit':'targetWidth' layers (the four AS-IS marks) compute xscale PER RUN as targetWidth / naturalWidthAtSize — always re-derive it from the live glyph metrics, never hard-code a captured xscale number for these; the font file is the source of truth.
'fit':'blend' layers (organic only) use a DECLARED xscale + trackingEm instead of a full fit-to-width stretch — see the organic mark's own note for why.
PRECISION: round path coordinates to 1 decimal on output (0.1 unit on a 150-unit box = 0.07% error, visually identical, ~66% smaller file than full float).

KNOWN BROKEN, ROOT-CAUSED (t2161, confirmed t2163): the organic mark's 'D' glyph traces with a corrupted inner counter path, so the shipped brand/MARK-ORGANIC-TRACED.svg visibly reads 'DOCS'. This is NOT an extraction/pipeline bug — t2163 re-fetched Sniglet ExtraBold (wght 800, this mark's declared weight) live and read its 'glyf' table directly: the D's own second contour is a genuine ~79x79-unit fragment against a ~610x723-unit outer contour (under 13% of the width), identical in both the API-subsetted and the full un-subsetted webfont. Sniglet REGULAR (wght 400)'s D, fetched and inspected the same way, has a normal ~61%-width counter — so this is specific to weight 800's own published outline data, not Sniglet as a family. fontTools is extracting exactly what the font file contains; there is nothing in this declaration or trace-wordmark.py to fix. Options are DESIGN decisions (a different declared weight, a different face, or leave organic on its old font-based render pending an upstream fix from the font's publisher) — not this file's or this script's to decide. See brand/README.md and WORK-LOG.md t2161+t2163.

studio.note: the engraved-nameplate bevel: each line is stamped TWICE, a light layer offset +dx/+dy behind a dark layer at the true position, same font/size/slant/fit both times.

organic.status: BROKEN, ROOT-CAUSED (t2163) — see the traps entry above and brand/README.md. Sniglet ExtraBold (weight 800, declared below) has a genuinely defective 'D' outline as published; Sniglet Regular (400) does not. This is upstream of trace-wordmark.py, not fixable by editing this declaration or the interpreter. index.html still shows the OLD font-request <text> render (Georgia italic, textLength=146), NOT this declaration — that is the correct state to remain in until a design decision is made (different weight/face, or wait on the font publisher).
organic.note: human-chosen 2026-08-22, from live specimens compared across Sniglet/Fredoka/Nunito (an upright, unsheared Sniglet was also compared and NOT chosen — round bowls shear worse than they read wrong upright, but the 9deg lean was kept to match futuristic/normal's own lean; steampunk is the only other upright mark, so this is not the odd one out). FLAT (no bevel/glow/gradient) — one layer per line, both Sniglet 800. 'fit':'blend' means: stretch glyphs by the declared xscale (NOT a full fit-to-targetWidth stretch — that was measured at ~2.09x and judged too distorting for Sniglet's round bowls), then add trackingEm*size of extra advance between each pair of glyphs (not after the last) until the line totals targetWidth.
